label: Maple Street Feeder 12 Lidar Extraction
comments: End-to-end example of a lidar/point-cloud extraction exported to SPIDAcalc: five connected locations, connected wires through the middle poles (connectedWire), field-measured sags supplying the tension data on every span (measuredSag), and terrain under every span (wireEndPoints[].terrainPoints, heights relative to the pole base). Span 3 crosses a creek, so its terrain profile dips. Connected items must agree: connected WEPs share a connectionId and have equal distances, opposite directions, and negated relative elevations; connected wires share client item, owner, usage group, tension group, and measuredSag. See doc/lidar_integration.md and the Connectivity section of doc/calc.md.

locations.label: MS-101
locations.comments: Deadend pole at the start of the run. Down guy and anchor resist the span tension toward MS-102.

locations.label: MS-102
locations.comments: Tangent pole. Through-running conductors are one wire per span, tied together with connectedWire.

locations.label: MS-103
locations.comments: Tangent pole with a distribution transformer. Primary is supported by a pole-top pin insulator.

wireEndPoints.comments: Creek crossing. Terrain points from ground classification show the channel under the span.

locations.label: MS-104
locations.comments: Tangent pole on the far side of the creek.

wireEndPoints.comments: Creek crossing. Terrain points from ground classification show the channel under the span.

locations.label: MS-105
locations.comments: Deadend pole at the end of the run. Down guy and anchor resist the span tension back toward MS-104.
